source.title: Gated Normalization Removal and Scale Anchoring in Pre-Norm Transformers
source.authors: Andrei Kanavalau; Carmen Amo Alonso; Sanjay Lall

record.tranche_reason: Tests a related normalization-removal question in pre-norm language transformers, outside the claim versions’ stated classification benchmarks and architectures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss trajectories for baseline and Internal-Taper (+aux), but gives no numeric training-loss values in the text. Validation losses, decoding throughput, and scale-anchoring results do not measure the claim’s training-classification-error outcome, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests gradual RMSNorm/LayerNorm removal and output-scale anchoring in language transformers. It does not test any stated version: in particular, V6 concerns batch normalization and the specific Fixup recipe, neither of which is evaluated. A related normalization experiment alone does not qualify as T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Internal tapering produces modest TinyStories validation-loss increases and competitive GPT-2 normalization-removal results. Final normalization acts as an output-scale anchor, whose stabilizing role the fixed-target scale loss partly replaces in the tested settings.
record.recipe_differences: Gated normalization removal and scale anchoring in pre-norm language transformers; evaluates language-modeling loss rather than classification error. The paper cites normalization and residual-network work as context.
record.method_sensitivity: Removing the final normalization without an explicit fixed-target scale anchor causes logit growth in the reported ablations; internal tapering with the final normalization retained is described as the most stable setting.

fits_no_version.finding: TinyStories baseline and Internal-Taper (+aux) have qualitatively similar training-loss trajectories when final RMSNorm is retained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal RMSNorm can be gradually tapered to fixed scalings in the tested depth-8 TinyStories transformers with auxiliary scale anchoring while preserving similar training-loss trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing final normalization without explicit anchoring produces logit growth; fixed-target scale anchoring suppresses it and reduces the gradient-magnitude separation between Internal-Taper and All-Taper.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final normalization provides output-scale control in the tested pre-norm transformers, and a fixed-target scale penalty can replace part of this role.

record.problems: The relevant training-loss comparison is shown in a figure and described qualitatively; numerical training-loss values are not stated. The experiments do not measure training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: Validation-loss results in Tables 1 and 3 do not measure training classification error. Table 2 measures decoding throughput, and the scale-anchoring results measure logit and gradient magnitudes; none are rows for the claim’s training-classification-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified plain-network and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats training classification error as the outcome required by every version; several versions concern speed, depth, or stability. Exclusion here rests on the actual interventions and questions tested, rather than on language-model loss alone. The paper discusses the original normalization and residual-network findings as background.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus residual convolutional networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; the paper does not vary depth or shortcut connections.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, and trainable depth under different initializations.
Learning-rate stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization’s effect on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup’s normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: Baseline and Internal-Taper (+aux)
rows.size_stated: TinyStories pre-norm transformers; widths 1M to 30M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-loss trajectories with internal normalizers tapered and final normalization retained versus baseline.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded regions indicate the 2.5–97.5 percentile range across seeds for each configuration.
rows.note: Authors state the trajectories are very similar; the text supplies no numeric training-loss values. The measure is language-modeling loss, not training classification error.
rows.check: The version links are correct. This comparison measures language-model training loss under internal RMSNorm tapering with auxiliary scale anchoring, not a stated version's effect. The text establishes qualitatively similar trajectories; missing numerical values alone would not make that qualitative finding indeterminate. The state applies to the claim versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
